title: Release a loaded spring platform under control
context: Removing a mechanical restraint can release stored spring energy. This unpowered prototype tests whether a robot supports a moving part during restraint removal and unloads it without a sudden upward motion.
setup: Use the official bimanual YAM station with the table at z 0.7475 m. x points forward. y points left. z points up. The blue fixture is rigid plastic and fixed to the table at root x 280 mm and y 0 mm and z at the tabletop. Its base is 120 mm by 140 mm by 8 mm. Two covered bar guides are centred at y negative 45 mm and positive 45 mm. Their top crosspieces are 50 mm by 14 mm by 14 mm centred 65 mm above the table. The moving platform is 80 mm by 70 mm by 12 mm with a 24 mm by 80 mm by 12 mm support tab toward positive y. Its mass is 40 g. At its lower stop the plate centre is 40 mm above the table. Its guided vertical travel is 60 mm. Its spring targets 60 mm of extension with stiffness 40 N per metre and damping 0.15 N seconds per metre and maximum force 3 N. The orange retaining bar is loose rigid plastic with mass 30 g. Its stem is 14 mm by 120 mm by 10 mm. Its handle is 30 mm by 30 mm by 20 mm. The stem root starts at x 280 mm and y 0 mm and z 51 mm above the table with zero yaw. The handle centre is 75 mm toward negative y and 5 mm above that root. A fixed white return pad is 70 mm by 180 mm by 1 mm centred at x 180 mm and y negative 190 mm and z 0.5 mm above the table. All local solids and joint anchors are listed in scene_inventory.json.
scoring: The entire episode scores zero if sampled platform speed ever exceeds 80 mm per second or the retaining bar drops more than 8 mm below the tabletop. Otherwise score 0.25 when the complete retaining bar is beyond y negative 55 mm. Score 0.5 when the bar is clear and platform extension is above 35 mm. Score 0.75 when the bar is clear and the platform extension is between 47 mm and 54 mm with speed below 10 mm per second and the bar is stored on its pad. For storage the complete bar must lie within x 145 mm to 215 mm and y negative 280 mm to negative 100 mm. Its bottom must be between negative 1 mm and positive 4 mm above the table. Its top must be below 40 mm. Bar translation must be below 10 mm per second and rotation below 0.1 radians per second. Score 1.0 for that completed state with both measured grippers open beyond 35 mm of travel. Full success must hold for one second. Checks run at 20 Hz. All other outcomes score zero. The highest currently satisfied partial credit is returned.
reset_notes: Return the platform to its lower stop while supporting it. Insert the retaining bar through both guides above the platform. Restore every root pose from scene_inventory.json. Nothing is consumed. Run one epoch per process with seed 0 and object_jitter=0.
fidelity: One rigid platform on an ideal vertical prismatic guide. A passive spring supplies upward force. The bar and guide covers have physical collision geometry. Contacts use simulator defaults with 1 mm compound contact offsets. Speed is sampled at 20 Hz. No deformation or fracture is modeled. This is a low mass unpowered analogue of controlled stored energy release.
instruction: Unload the spring fixture without allowing its platform to snap upward. Support the blue platform before withdrawing the orange retaining bar. Keep platform speed below 80 mm per second. Let it rise to its unloaded position under control. Put the bar on the white return pad. Finish with both grippers open. This is an unpowered test fixture.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 120 seconds of control time.
